conventions.convention: The momentum residual is w_t + (w·∇)w + ρ₀⁻¹∇q − νΔw − f. The Jacobian has entries ∂_j w_i; boundary traces are classical restrictions of neighborhood extensions.
The wall comparison uses divergence-free fields with identical full wall traces. The explicit channel lift is (a(t)(1−y/h)+b(t)y/h,0,0), exclusively for the specified tangential defects.
Volume L² norms use ordinary, unnormalized volume measure, including one cell in the periodic channel. L(t) is the supremum of |ζ·D_xu ξ| over positions and Euclidean unit vectors.
Countable Choice is explicitly assumed for the bounded-domain divergence theorem application.
The vertical coordinate points upward; the bottom is z=−h and the reference surface is z=0. The dynamic condition is φ_t+gη−(σ/ρ)Δ_Hη=0, with σ≥0, and velocity is ∇φ with no added uniform component.

The capillary mode uses the positive frequency, wavelength λ=2π/k, and periodic sine/cosine values of a representative-dependent real phase. Energy is integrated over one horizontal cell, including the finite transverse span.
The wave claims are exact deductions within the linear mathematical model, with no nonlinear approximation, convergence, or empirical-observation assertion.

load_bearing.statement: Defines the full forced momentum residual, common-wall comparison and supplied divergence-free wall lift; independently defines the periodic capillary-gravity potential equations Δφ=0, φ_z(−h)=0, η_t=φ_z(0), and φ_t(0)+gη−(σ/ρ)Δ_Hη=0, with the stated classical regularity and positive parameters, allowing σ=0.

For h,g,ρ,k,L_y>0, σ≥0 and a∈ℝ, the displayed smooth periodic mode solves the linear capillary-gravity equations with positive frequency ω_σ²=(gk+(σ/ρ)k³)tanh(kh). At σ=0 it is exactly the finite-depth gravity-wave mode. For any T>0 and any solution with the stated C¹-in-time, C²-in-space neighborhood-extension regularity, the displayed cell energy is nonnegative and constant on [0,T].

Assuming Countable Choice, the stated classical divergence-free exact and comparison solutions on a bounded connected C² domain with common wall trace satisfy ‖v(t)−u(t)‖₂ ≤ exp(A(t))(‖v(0)−u(0)‖₂ + ∫₀ᵗ exp(−A(s))‖r(s)‖₂ ds), where r=R(v,q) and A(t)=∫₀ᵗL(s)ds. The same estimate holds on the periodic channel with common wall traces; the specified tangential lift yields the displayed corrected residual and triangle-inequality bound for w−u.

concerns.concern: The source metadata names “Erik Wiedemann, Lecture Notes: Navier–Stokes Equations.” The linked PDF title page identifies Emil Wiedemann, edited by Jack Skipper. This is an author-name error; the cited relative-energy material is present. Source checked: https://www.math.fau.de/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/wiedemann-NSE-final.pdf, PDF page 1.

The source metadata repeats “Erik Wiedemann” for the lecture notes whose linked title page identifies Emil Wiedemann. Correct the attribution consistently with the model definition. This does not affect the locally supplied energy proof.

seams_checked.note: Compared the periodic solenoidal residual definition and residual-error theorem with the assigned bounded-domain argument. The latter supplies its own full-pressure energy proof and does not incorrectly transfer periodic face cancellation to physical walls. The page prerequisite is contextual; no assigned item cites the periodic theorem as a black-box bounded-domain result.

The Cartesian operator conventions agree. The capillary proof uses the gravity mode at rescaled time and scales its potential by the same positive factor, retaining the exact gravity-mode hypotheses. The σ=0 frequency, elevation and potential coefficient agree with thm-fd-x03, including a=0.

The physical postulate explicitly identifies mathematical σ with physical γ and matches the periods and boundary signs. Its stricter γ>0 is permitted. Its formulation notes supply the neighborhood extension and explain why the kinematic equation upgrades η to the mathematical supplier's C¹-in-time C²-in-space class. The downstream dispersion theorem proves its broader complex-mode iff locally rather than attributing that stronger conclusion to the assigned explicit real-mode theorem. Conditional physical scope is preserved.
